newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end higher on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end higher on speculative buying.

text.p: - Shenzhen's B share index ended higher on Monday in line with a sharp rise in the A share market, boosted by speculative institutional demand for a range of cheap-priced counters, brokers said.
The B share index gained 3.01 points or 2.12 percent to end at 145.01, on volume of 15.95 million shares worth HK$77.56 million, compared with HK$47.68 million last Friday.
The A share index advanced 9.70 points or 2.88 percent to close at 346.94, with turnover swelling to 5.20 billion yuan against the previous session's 3.71 billion yuan.

The B share gain was linked to the strong performance of the A share market, which was still heavily influenced by talk that a further cut in bank interest rates or in bank reserve requirements is possible later this year, a broker said.
"Investor confidence has recovered slightly after moderate rises over the past three sessions and technical charts appear good for further buying on the back of today's advances," a trader said.
But he said that with third-line issue among the best performers today, trading remained quite speculative and volatile.

Jiangling Motors, the best performing B share, rose HK$0.23 or 7.77 percent to HK$3.19 on volume of 5167,300 shares. Property concern China Vanke followed with a gain of HK$0.29 to HK$5.54 on thin trade of 196,749 shares.

Changan Automobile was the most active share on volume of 2.26 million shares and added HK$0.10 to HK$4.61. Hotelier Dadonghai edged up HK$0.07 to HK$3.72 on the session's second most active trade of 848,500 shares.
Television maker Konka, the day's sole loser, fell HK$0.05 to HK$8.13, with only 9,901 shares changing hands.
On the A share market, retailer Tianjin Leadar closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 6.00 yuan on speculative institutional buying, brokers said. Jiangling Motors followed suit, ending at 5.91 yuan.
